# odyssey-015 — new rendering candidates (Odyssey 4.113–218)

New formulas / noun-epithet pairs not yet in `conventions.md`'s house table, chosen with the same
care and kept consistent every time they occur within this part. Same row format as the house table.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| χλαῖναν πορφυρέην ἄντ’ ὀφθαλμοῖιν ἀνασχών/ἀνασχὼν (whole-phrase gesture, 4.115 = 4.154) | "his purple cloak before his eyes having raised" | "raising his purple cloak before his eyes" | "mantle" (kept "cloak" for χλαῖνα throughout), "crimson"/"dark-red" for πορφύρεος (kept plainly "purple") |
| Ἀρτέμιδι χρυσηλακάτῳ ἐικυῖα (simile for a woman, 4.122) | "like to Artemis of the golden distaff" | "like Artemis of the golden distaff" | "golden-shafted" (ἠλακάτη is a spindle/distaff, not an arrow — kept apart from Artemis's bow), "golden-spindled" (less natural in English) |
| τὸν/τὴν δ’ αὖ [Name] [patronymic] ἀντίον ηὔδα (reply-formula: name + patronymic + ἀντίον ηὔδα, here Πεισίστρατος, 4.155) | "Him then in turn spoke Peisistratus, Nestor's son, face to face:" | "Then Peisistratus, son of Nestor, spoke to him in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for τὸν/τὴν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα); kept on the pattern already fixed for τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύμαχος Πολύβου πάϊς ἀντίον ηὔδα and τὸν δ’ Εὐηνορίδης Λειώκριτος ἀντίον ηὔδα |
| Ἀτρεΐδη Μενέλαε διοτρεφές, ὄρχαμε λαῶν (full vocative address line, 4.156) | "Atreus' son, Menelaus, Zeus-nurtured, chief of the people," | "Son of Atreus, Menelaus, Zeus-nurtured, chief of the people," | naming him "Menelaus" alone and dropping the patronymic or the titles; ὄρχαμε λαῶν kept distinct in wording from the already-fixed ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν ("chief of men") since λαός and ἀνήρ are different nouns |
| κυνῶπις (Helen's self-reproach, 4.145, of herself) | "dog-faced" | "shameless" | "bitch" (too coarse for the register and not what the compound says), "shameless-eyed" (loses the plain κύων), translating away the self-blame entirely |
| Ἀργείη Ἑλένη, Διὸς ἐκγεγαυῖα (whole phrase, 4.184) | "Argive Helen, sprung of Zeus," | "Argive Helen, the daughter sprung from Zeus," | "born of Zeus" (flattens the perfect participle's sense of 'having come to be'), "Zeus-born" (reserved for the distinct adjective διογενής), "child of Zeus" (reserved for the noun-phrase Διὸς θυγάτηρ, used of Athena; here Homer uses a participle, not θυγάτηρ, so the two are kept apart) |

## Judgment calls flagged but NOT added above (each occurs only once in this part, so does not yet
meet the "plainly recurs" bar, but a future drafter meeting them again should look here first)

- **κλισίη** (4.123) vs. **κλισμός** (4.136): rendered "seat" and "chair" respectively, so that
  English keeps the two Greek nouns for a place to sit apart, even though both describe similar
  furniture; κλισμός is the more specific word for a chair with a back.
- **γέρας** (4.197, "τοῦτό νυ καὶ γέρας οἶον ὀιζυροῖσι βροτοῖσιν"): rendered "due, honour" with a
  note on its ironic use here (the mourning-rites as the only "privilege" left to the unhappy dead
  and their kin). Not logged as a fixed formula since it is a single occurrence, not a recurring
  epithet, but the ironic sense is worth carrying forward if the word recurs in this same context.
- **νάσσα** (4.174, causative aorist of ναίω, "I would have settled [him in a city]") vs. **ἔναιε**
  (4.126, intransitive, "he dwelt"): both from the same verb ναίω but used transitively/causatively
  and intransitively; flagged so a later drafter does not conflate the two senses under one gloss.
- **ἤλθεθ’** (= ἤλθετε, 4.146): a genuine Homeric "apostrophe," switching from third-person Ἀχαιοί to
  a second-person verb mid-clause, rendered by keeping "you Achaeans" explicit in both `l` and `i`
  rather than smoothing it back to the third person. Worth watching for the same device elsewhere in
  the poem (it is best known from single-hero apostrophes such as Patroclus in the Iliad; here it is
  extended to a collective addressee).
- **ὢ πόποι, ἦ μάλα δὴ φίλου ἀνέρος υἱὸς ἐμὸν δῶ / ἵκεθ’** (4.169–170): not logged as a fixed
  reply-opening since it is built from already-fixed pieces (ὢ πόποι) plus ordinary vocabulary; no
  new formula needed.
